Subject: Private deployment: VPC peering & endpoint validation — cutover cadence

Hi Samira —

Nice catching up last week. Per our playbook, I'm outlining the proposed cutover cadence and what we need from Helios NetOps to validate VPC peering and private endpoints before we hand off the on-prem package. High level:

- Target cutover window: Thu May 27, 00:00 - 04:00 PT (low-traffic)
- Preflight validation: Tue May 25, 09:00 - 11:00 PT (mutual test window)
- Teams required on the call: Helios NetOps (Tom + 1), Helios Security (as needed), Redwood CS (me + Ben), Redwood Infra (Monica)

Attachments included: vpc_peer_config_v1.yaml (proposed routes and ASNs), redwood_onprem_package_v1.2.tar.gz (installer + README), network-test-plan.xlsx (test matrix and expected results). Please review the VPC CIDR mapping and confirm whether your egress NAT will be applied at the transit gateway or at the application subnets — that determines the source IPs we'll expect for the endpoint allowlist.

Action items for Helios:
1) Confirm the cutover window or propose an alternate 4-hour window.
2) Send the transit gateway/public IPs to be allowlisted for private endpoints.
3) Identify the engineer(s) who will run connectivity tests on May 25.

If you confirm today, I’ll loop in Monica for a short runbook review and Ben to coordinate the test harness.

Thanks,
Rishi

Quick note: I’ll assemble the harness and test matrix. A few technical notes up front that we should call out in the checklist:

- If Helios NATs at TGW, our healthcheck IPs will be the TGW EIPs. We should add a step to verify the expected source IPs from both the endpoint and the onprem package during the preflight.
- We need a plan for asymmetric routing — if Helios has asymmetric return paths, packet capture on both sides will be required.
- For the installer, we currently support two modes:
  * NAT-aware (default) — assumes outbound IPs will be the TGW EIPs
  * Host-preserve — preserves original host IP if you push the package onto a host behind the TGW (requires different firewall rules)

I’ll attach the trimmed checklist and a preflight runbook draft before EOD.

Subject: Risk register + runbook notes for Helios cutover

Tom / Samira / Team —

Thanks for the quick responses. I pulled together a short risk register and a couple of runbook notes that will help the preflight stay focused. See inline highlights below and I’ve attached the config snippet we intend to apply if TGW NAT is confirmed.

Top risks (mitigation):
- Unexpected IP mismatch (mitigation: verify TGW EIPs and add temporary allowlist entries during preflight)
- Asymmetric routing (mitigation: simultaneous packet captures + roll-back plan)
- Installer permission errors on first-run (mitigation: pre-provision account with sudo and provide check commands)

Proposed quick agenda for May 25 preflight (60-90 mins):
1) Introductions & roles (5 mins)
2) Confirm TGW EIPs and route tables (10 mins)
3) Run connectivity checks (30 mins)
4) Validate private endpoint access + TLS handshake (15 mins)
5) Capture results & risk decision (10-20 mins)

If that looks good, I’ll finalize the runbook and attach the vpc_peer_config_v1.yaml as the authoritative reference for the preflight.

Monica Patel
